title: Half-wave wire dipole at 10 GHz fed by a lumped port: power balance and directivity
source: Energy conservation (the power the port delivers is the power radiated through the Huygens box, the structure being lossless) and the directivity of a half-wave dipole with a sinusoidal current, D = (4/Cin(2π)) [cos(π/2 cos θ)/sin θ]² (C. A. Balanis, Antenna Theory, 4th ed., Wiley 2016, §4.6)

quantities.quantity: radiated power over the power the port delivers
quantities.reason: two independent integrals of one solution, ½ Re(V I*) at the gap and ½ Re ∮ E × H* · dS round the antenna: 0.995 at four elements per wavelength (the layer's own absorption and the box's quadrature)
the closed form assumes a thin wire's sinusoidal current; this one is λ/60 thick with a 1 mm gap: +2.1 %
